Server Policy workspace

The FortiWeb Server Policy workspace — list, filter, inspect, edit, create, enable, disable and delete the server policies of the selected FortiWeb, served from SATOM's local copy of the configuration.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view network.edit network.apply protection.edit protection.apply users.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy (URL /workspace/<appliance_id>)

What is it?#

The Server Policy workspace is the main FortiWeb page in SATOM. It lists every server policy of the selected FortiWeb, opens each one in a FortiWeb-style form, and lets an operator change, create, enable, disable, delete, clone or migrate policies. The list and the detail view are read from SATOM's local copy of the configuration, so browsing does not load the appliance; the device is contacted when you press Refresh from device, save a change, or ask for live health.

What does it do?#

  • Lists the policies in FortiWeb's own layout for the device's firmware build: FortiWeb's toolbar and columns in FortiWeb's order, plus a checkbox per row. With no GUI layout imported (no knowledge pack yet), the list draws FortiWeb 7.6's default columns with the same toolbar.
  • Filters the list in the browser by name (Name or /regex/…) and, under Filters, by VIP, back-end pool, back-end server IP, certificate type and status. Text filters accept a plain substring or a /regex/.
  • Shows a badge with the age of the local data and pulls fresh configuration on demand with Refresh from device (⟳).
  • Edit opens FortiWeb's Edit Server Policy dialog for the policy's protocol. With no GUI layout imported, it opens SATOM's policy view instead: the service topology (VIP → policy → pool → real servers), the full policy form, the virtual server's VIP rows, the server pool and its members, content routing rules and the raw configuration.
  • Saves only the fields you changed, after showing you the exact request.
  • Create New opens FortiWeb's Create New menu, or SATOM's New Server Policy form when no layout is imported. Either creates a new policy together with its objects in one dependency-ordered run.
  • Runs Clone, Clone to, Migrate to, Enable, Disable and Delete from the toolbar on the selected or ticked rows (see Cloning & migrating policies for the first three).
  • Marks each policy that has been cloned or migrated with a counter; hovering it shows the Clone history (where, when, by whom, and why a copy failed).

Requirements#

  • At least one FortiWeb registered in SATOM (see Appliances).
  • A selected device. When the FortiWeb ADOM is active and no device has been chosen yet, the workspace redirects you to the Service Diagram to pick one.
  • Data in SATOM's local store. A device that was never synchronised shows the badge no local data — refresh; press Refresh from device once.
  • The VIP / IP… and Backend server IP… filters need a deep capture (run from Analysis).

Permissions#

protection.view opens the list, the detail page, the Check live health probe and the reference dropdowns, for every device you can see. Devices in maintenance mode are hidden unless you hold appliances.view_maintenance.

Every action that writes or reads the whole device — Refresh from device, saving a form, creating an object with ＋, Create New, From a line profile, and every toolbar action on the selected rows (Clone, Clone to, Migrate to, Enable, Disable, Delete) — requires the legacy config_write permission. Any granular key that implies it unlocks these actions; the natural ones for server policies are network.edit, network.apply, protection.edit and protection.apply. The Operator and Administrator profiles have them; the Viewer profile does not.

The AppID selector of the New Server Policy form is shown only with users.manage; a create request that names an AppID without it is refused before anything is written.

🔑Permission — What a viewer sees

Without config_write the list shows no Create New, From a line profile or Refresh from device button, and none of the Clone, Clone to, Migrate to, Enable, Disable and Delete buttons. SATOM's policy view shows Read-only: changing this policy needs the config_write permission. and hides its save and create controls. Nothing can be written.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: write controls are hidden without config_write, Refresh from device now needs config_write, the New Server Policy form has a Web Protection Profile field and a working AppID selector, and Change Appliance opens the Architecture map.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: Server Policy is an entry of FortiWeb's own menu, FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy; the Loadbalancer group is gone. While no GUI layout is imported for the device's build, it is the FortiWeb group's only entry (FortiWeb → Server Policy). The list is drawn in FortiWeb's layout, and Clone, Clone to, Migrate to, Enable, Disable and Delete are toolbar buttons that act on the selected or ticked rows. SATOM's classic list, with its ⋮ row menu, bulk bar and counters, is gone; /web/workspace/<id> opens the new list.

How to use#

Open the policy list#

  1. In the sidebar, open FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy.
  2. The list for the currently selected FortiWeb opens. The header shows the device name, its address and firmware; the toolbar shows the local-data badge.
  3. Click a row to select it; double-click it, press Enter or click Edit to open the policy.

To work on another FortiWeb, press Change Appliance. It opens the Service Diagram, where you pick the device.

Filter the list#

  1. Type into Name or /regex/… in the toolbar, or open Filters below it and type into VIP / IP…, Backend pool… or Backend server IP…. Plain text is a case-insensitive substring; /pol-.*-prod/ is a regular expression (case-insensitive unless you add flags).
  2. Narrow with Any certificate (Local, Multi (SNI), Let's Encrypt, None) and All Status (Enabled, Disabled).
  3. The × button clears every filter.

A filter box turns red when the pattern is invalid, longer than 200 characters, or too slow to evaluate; that box is then ignored until you edit it. Filtering never contacts SATOM or the device.

Refresh from device#

  1. Press Refresh from device (needs config_write).
  2. SATOM reads the whole configuration from the appliance, stores it and returns to the list with Refreshed from <device>: <detail>.

Inspect and edit a policy#

With a GUI layout for the device's build, Edit opens FortiWeb's Edit Server Policy dialog: fields show and hide as you edit, Save shows Review the change, and Apply to <device> writes it, through the same gates listed below. The steps that follow describe SATOM's policy view, which Edit opens when no layout has been imported.

  1. Open a policy. The header shows its status, deployment mode and protocol; the name is marked name locked because it is the object key.
  2. Optional: press Check live health in Service Topology & Backend Health to colour each back-end UP, DOWN or N/A (no health check) from the device's live status. The page also works without it.
  3. Change fields in Server Policy Configuration. Sections and fields appear and disappear as in the FortiWeb GUI (for example the content-routing card only shows in HTTP Content Routing mode). Changed fields are highlighted and the bar counts N unsaved change(s).
  4. Press the section's save button (Save policy, Save VIP, Save pool, or Save on a back-end row).
  5. Review the Confirm change to the live device dialog: one row per field with Was and New, and the raw request.
  6. Press Apply to device. The toast reads Saved to device.

Before anything is sent — on the preview and on the apply — a save passes the same gates as the object editor, in the same order:

  1. Template lock — a template-managed Web Protection Profile stays read-only here; the save is refused and points to the Template Library, where the change is made.
  2. Edit lease — another user's edit lease on the object refuses the write ("<name>" is being edited by <user>. Take over the edit lock first; nothing was sent to the device.). A row of an inline table (VIP row, pool member, content-routing row) is checked against its parent's lease.
  3. Reference check — a reference to an object the device does not have is refused with the field name.
  4. Build compatibility — what this exact firmware build rejects is refused, and fields the build lacks are stripped.

After a successful write SATOM releases your edit lease on the object. The write itself re-reads what it touched from the device, refreshes SATOM's copy from that read and checks that the device holds what was sent; a value the device accepted but did not keep is recorded in the audit log as config.update.not_applied. No second read follows the save. In the FortiWeb-style Server Policy dialog, a save whose copy could not be refreshed says Saved on the device; the SATOM copy refreshes on the next sync.

Reference fields are dropdowns filled with the objects configured on the device. ✎ opens the selected object in a side panel; ＋ creates a new one. The ＋ next to the Web Protection Profile opens a small dialog that can clone the settings of an existing profile (Clone settings from). Manage VIP rows…, Manage members… and Members… open the virtual server or pool in the full object editor (see Server objects).

Create a new server policy#

With a GUI layout for the device's build, Create New opens FortiWeb's Create New menu; pick the kind of policy and fill FortiWeb's dialog, which starts from FortiWeb's defaults. An entry marked conditional may be hidden on this device by a setting SATOM cannot see. A policy with no HTTP, HTTPS or HTTP/3 service is refused before anything is written. With no layout imported, Create New opens SATOM's New Server Policy form:

  1. On the list, press Create New.
  2. Fill Policy name (required). Optionally fill Virtual Server name and add rows with ＋ Add VIP, and Server Pool name with ＋ Add member rows.
  3. Set the fields in Policy settings. Choose the profile in the Web Protection Profile group.
  4. Administrators (with users.manage) can choose an AppID from the catalog (see AppIDs).
  5. Press Preview (dry-run). The page lists every object that would be created, in order, with its exact body. Create on device is enabled only after a preview.
  6. Press Create on device. Every step is re-read from the device: a step the device accepted but does not hold as sent fails, and the run stops (see Troubleshooting). On success the page shows ✓ Created. and a link to open the policy. When an AppID was chosen, the new policy is bound to it and the binding is recorded in the audit log. A preview binds nothing.

For a guided build that also reserves the address, publishes DNS and issues the certificate, use From a line profile — see New Server Policy from a line.

Enable, disable or delete#

  1. Select a row, or tick several rows (the toolbar counts N selected).
  2. Press Enable, Disable or Delete in the toolbar.
  3. Press Preview (dry-run). For Delete, the preview lists what WILL BE DELETED and what WILL BE KEPT, with the policies a kept object is shared with or the reason it is never deleted (for example Web Protection Profile (never auto-deleted)). The dialog says it up front: objects used only by this policy (virtual server, VIP, server pool…) are deleted with it; Web Protection Profiles, certificates, services and objects shared with other policies are kept.
  4. Press Apply for real. The dialog closes and the run continues as a background job with a progress toast (see Jobs).

Apply for real stays disabled until a preview has succeeded.

Configuration#

New Server Policy form

Field Description Required Example
Policy name Name of the server policy (object key). Yes pol-shop
Virtual Server name Creates a virtual server and binds it to the policy. No vs-shop
VIP rows vip, interface, use-interface-ip, status per row; created under the virtual server. No vip-shop, port1
Server Pool name Creates a server pool and binds it to the policy. No pool-shop
Pool members Type (physical, domain, sdn), IP / Domain, Port, Weight, SSL, Status. No 192.0.2.21, 8080
Web Protection Profile Profile the new policy is bound to; part of the policy body. No wpp-shop
AppID AppID the policy is bound to after a successful create. Shown only with users.manage. No — none —
Policy settings The policy fields grouped as in the GUI. Blank fields are not sent. No —

Filters

Field Matches Needs deep capture
Name or /regex/… Policy name No
VIP / IP… VIP addresses of the policy Yes
Backend pool… Server pool name No
Backend server IP… Pool member addresses Yes
Any certificate Certificate type of the policy: Local, Multi (SNI), Let's Encrypt, None No
All Status Enabled / Disabled No

Example#

🧪Example — Take a policy out of service for maintenance

On fweb-01, the policy pol-shop serves www.example.com.

  1. Filter with /^pol-shop$/.
  2. Select the row, press Disable, then Preview (dry-run): the preview shows the single status: disable request.
  3. Apply for real. The toast tracks the job; the bell notification reads Disable: 1/1 server policy ok.
  4. Press Refresh from device to see the row turn Disabled.

Result#

  • Field saves and object creations are written through SATOM's audited write path: each change is recorded with a before/after snapshot in the change history and the audit log.
  • Row and bulk actions run as a background job titled <Action> — N server policies on <device>. Each policy gets an audit entry (policy.enable, policy.delete, …) and the run gets a summary entry; the user who started it receives a notification.
  • Re-binding a policy's Web Protection Profile marks the exceptions written for the old profile as stale; deleting a policy removes its exceptions from SATOM (see Exceptions).
  • A save or a create re-reads what it wrote into SATOM's local copy. Use Refresh from device for changes made outside SATOM.

Troubleshooting#

"VIP / backend filters need a deep capture"#

Possible causes - No deep capture exists for this device, so VIP and back-end data are not in the local store.

Solution 1. Run a deep capture for the device from Analysis. 2. Reload the Server Policy page.

Verification — the badge disappears and the VIP / IP… filter narrows the list.

"No server policies cached for this device. Use Refresh from device."#

Possible causes - The device has no server policies. - The local store is empty for this device.

Solution 1. Press Refresh from device (⟳). 2. If the flash message reports an error, check the device's reachability and credentials on its appliance page.

Verification — the toolbar counts the expected number of policies.

"Refresh failed (Error ID: …)"#

Possible causes - The device could not be read (unreachable, authentication failure, license lock). The last good local copy is kept.

Solution 1. Open the device's appliance page and test the connection. 2. Quote the error ID to your administrator; it identifies the log entry.

Verification — a new refresh reports Refreshed from <device>: ….

The save buttons and the policy actions are missing#

Possible causes - Your profile lacks every key that implies config_write: the list shows no Create New, Clone, Enable, Disable or Delete button, and SATOM's policy view says Read-only: changing this policy needs the config_write permission.

Solution 1. Ask an administrator for network.edit or another key listed under Permissions.

Verification — the save buttons appear and the Confirm change to the live device dialog opens.

Save refused with <field>: "<value>" — <reason>#

Possible causes - A reference field names an object the device does not have. SATOM checks references before writing instead of letting the device answer with a bare -651.

Solution 1. Pick an existing object from the dropdown, or create it with ＋. 2. If the dropdown is stale, press Refresh from device.

Verification — the dialog opens and Apply to device returns Saved to device.

"Live probe failed: …"#

Possible causes - The device is offline or license-locked, or refused the status query.

Solution 1. The page itself keeps working from the local copy; retry later. 2. Check the device on its appliance page.

Verification — the message changes to N of M back-end(s) matched live status.

"Server Pool failed: …" after Create on device#

Possible causes - One object in the chain was refused (duplicate name, missing reference). - The device accepted a step but the re-read does not find what was sent (the error then says the device accepted the write but does not hold it — … and names the field and the value the device kept).

Solution 1. Read the result under the error: applied lists every step with its outcome, rolled_back the objects this run deleted again (the FortiWeb-style dialog names them after undone:). A failed run undoes the top-level objects it created (virtual server, server pool, and a step the device accepted but did not apply), newest first; VIP rows and pool members go with their parent. Each delete is audited. 2. An object whose undo failed ("ok": false under rolled_back) is still on the device: delete it from Server objects. 3. Fix the cause and run Create on device again.

Verification — the policy opens from the list after a refresh.

"… is being edited by …. Take over the edit lock first; nothing was sent to the device."#

Possible causes - Another user holds the edit lease on the policy, or on the object the row you are saving belongs to.

Solution 1. Wait until the other user finishes, or take over the edit lock (see Locks).

Verification — the preview opens and Apply to device saves.

Advanced#

Advanced Data sources and freshness

The list reads the policy cache; the detail page prefers the deep capture (policy, virtual server with VIP rows, pool with members, protection profile and content routing). If a policy has no deep capture, the detail page reads the device live, and if that fails it shows the last cached copy with a warning that names its age. The reference dropdowns read the device first and fall back to cached object names when the device does not answer.

Advanced How Delete decides what to remove

Delete deletes the server policy first, then each object that only this policy uses (for example its virtual server, server pool, health check or content-routing policy). Objects used by another policy are kept and listed with the policies that share them. Web Protection Profiles and all WAF sub-profiles, certificates, services, SSL cipher groups, replacement message groups, v-zones and system VIP objects are always kept. Sub-tables such as VIP rows and pool members disappear with their parent. If the device answers "in use" for an object, it is reported as kept rather than failed. If the policy itself cannot be deleted, nothing else is touched.

Advanced What a save sends

A save sends only the changed fields, wrapped as FortiWeb expects, to the allow-listed configuration endpoint of the policy, pool, VIP row, pool member, content routing row or a referenced object. The first request is always a dry run that returns the exact body; the write happens only after you press Apply to device.

Advanced Policy links

Administrators can add buttons to the detail page under Settings → Policy Links. Each link is filled with the policy's own values (policy, device, VIP, port, pool, virtual server, protection profile); a link that names an empty value is not shown. See Settings.

Advanced FortiADC devices

If the selected device is a FortiADC, the list shows its virtual servers read live from the device, and Refresh from device answers Refresh is FortiWeb-only for now.
